# PRD 004: Copilot cache proxy

**Schema**: pij/prd · **Source**: 004-copilot-cache-proxy.dd.json · **Sections**: 8

| status | draft |
| updated | 2026-11-18 |

| summary | pij-spawned Copilot seats on Claude models get a 1-hour prompt cache through a local proxy that pij runs, so waking an idle seat no longer rebuilds its whole context. Anything not ready means the seat launches as plain Copilot, with the reason in its receipt. |

<a id="why"></a>

## Why

Claude seats on Copilot keep a 5-minute prompt cache. A pij message that wakes a seat idle longer than that rebuilds 200k to 450k tokens of context as cache writes, at 1.25x the input price. From 11 to 17 Nov 2026 that was about 45% of the fleet's model cost (`docs/how/prompt-cache-cost.md`, takin). OMP has its own 1-hour setting; Copilot CLI has none, because a server-side A/B test picks its TTL. A 200-line POC proxy (`~/pi-hacking/copilot-ttl-proxy`) that adds `ttl: "1h"` to every `cache_control` proved it: a turn sent after 6.5 minutes idle read 36,285 tokens from cache and wrote 49.

<a id="actors"></a>

## Actors

| id | name | need |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a-operator | operator | Pay less for idle seats, with nothing to configure beyond naming an account, and never a broken seat. |
| a-seat | seat | Run normally whether the proxy is on, off or failing. |
| a-prime | prime | Know which seats are proxied, and hear once when that changes or fails. |

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

| id | goal |
| --- | --- |
| g-1 | A proxied Copilot Claude seat woken after more than 5 minutes idle reads its context from cache, not rebuilds it. |
| g-2 | The proxy never breaks a seat: if it isn't proven ready at spawn, the seat runs plain Copilot. |

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non goals

| id | text |
| --- | --- |
| n-1 | OMP seats. They keep their own 1-hour cache setting and never use the proxy. |
| n-2 | Non-Claude models. A seat on a GPT or other model runs plain. |
| n-3 | Storing credentials. The token lives only in the proxy's memory. |
| n-4 | Multi-user machines. This Mac has one human account; doctor warns if that changes. |

| req-13 | Right model id and full context | A proxied seat reaches Copilot with a model id the API serves, and with its full context window. Copilot's API rejects OMP-style `-1m` selectors (`claude-opus-5.5-1m` gives 400 `model_not_supported`), while the base id already serves 1M. So the proxy maps any `*-1m` model to its base id before forwarding. The spawn sets `COPILOT_PROVIDER_MODEL_ID` to the base id and `COPILOT_PROVIDER_MAX_PROMPT_TOKENS` to that model's `max_prompt_tokens` from the account's `/models`. A Claude model the account's `/models` doesn't list launches plain, with the reason. | seat | must | [ ] planned | Test matrix row 22: seats spawned as `claude-opus-5.5` and as `claude-opus-5.5-1m` both get 200s, their status bars show a 1.0M window, the proxy log shows the base id, and only 1-hour cache writes appear. | spike REPORT.md addendum (takin, spike/004-cache-proxy 6566e91f) | — | — |

<a id="open-questions"></a>

## Open questions

| id | question | default | answer | status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| q-01 | Which token does Copilot's `/v1/messages` accept from the proxy (the gh OAuth token itself, or a session token exchanged from it), and how long does it live? | The gh OAuth token directly, as in the POC. If it's a session token, the proxy exchanges it and refreshes per req-03. | The `gho_` OAuth token from `gh auth token --user` is accepted directly by `&lt;endpoints.api&gt;/v1/messages`, including the enterprise host for a managed (EMU) account. It has no expiry: GitHub sends no expiration header, and the `copilot_internal/v2/token` exchange returns 403 for gh's OAuth client. So the token is refreshed only on a 401 (req-03). Evidence: spike REPORT.md, branch spike/004-cache-proxy 9a397862. | answered |
| q-02 | Inside the daemon, or a same-binary sidecar? | Sidecar unless the bounce test shows Copilot retries a refused connection and finishes the turn. | A same-binary sidecar: `pij-rs cache-proxy`, with its own LaunchAgent and its own loopback port, holding the token in its own memory. Ruled by the prime (far-jackal, 2026-11-18). A measured `just bounce-rs` closed the daemon's listener for 567 ms, well inside Copilot's ~20 s retry for a refused connection (spike q-02). But a bounce still cuts in-flight streams, which run for minutes, and the daemon drains for at most 15 s and bounces several times a day. A sidecar never bounces with the daemon. The daemon and doctor report its health and counters. | answered |
| q-03 | Port and config keys. | 127.0.0.1:7471; `copilot.account`; a machine-wide `copilot.cache_proxy = off` switch. | Port 127.0.0.1:7471. pij has no generic config store, so the proxy has its own file, `~/.pij-rs/cache-proxy.toml` (`account`, `enabled`), written only by `pij-rs cache-proxy account &lt;login&gt;` and `pij-rs cache-proxy off\|on` (blueprint 003, d-5). | answered |
